notes: Tracks deployable AMD Ryzen AI Embedded P100 platforms rather than treating processor TOPS as equivalent to LLM token throughput.
Memory-bandwidth figures marked theoretical are derived from advertised memory data rates and channel width, not measured application bandwidth.
No stable public unit pricing was found for these industrial platforms during this pass; quote/channel-dependent availability is preserved instead of inventing prices.

hardware.release_status: production shipments targeted from July 2026; current AMD product page recommends the part for new designs
hardware.llm_suitability: Good low-power host/edge SoC candidate when paired with sufficient memory. CPU/GPU inference and supported ROCm/Vulkan paths are more general than the NPU; XDNA2 TOPS must not be converted directly to GGUF tokens/s.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Platform-dependent. Boards with 96-128GB RAM can hold many 30B-70B class quantized models in system memory, but practical decode speed will be constrained by memory bandwidth and backend maturity.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: GGUF quantization is practical through CPU and compatible GPU backends; NPU execution requires supported/compiled XDNA2 software paths and is not arbitrary GGUF acceleration.

pricing.note: AMD does not publish a retail unit price for the embedded SoC.

hardware.product: MIO-5380 with AMD Ryzen AI Embedded P185
hardware.memory_type: dual-channel DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM with sideband ECC
hardware.memory_bandwidth_note: Derived theoretical peak: DDR5-5600 x 128-bit aggregate dual-channel width / 8. Not a measured LLM bandwidth result.
storage: 2x M.2 M-key 2280 PCIe Gen4 x4 NVMe
interfaces: MCIO PCIe Gen4 x4 on selected SKU
hardware.llm_suitability: Strong compact DC-powered edge host when configured with 96-128GB RAM. Best suited to CPU/iGPU quantized inference, orchestration, embeddings, and supported NPU workloads; dual-channel DDR5 bandwidth will limit very large-model decode.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 128GB capacity can store many 70B-class 4-bit weights with room for runtime overhead, but fit does not imply fast generation. 7B-30B-class quantized models are the more practical general-purpose range.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: GGUF via CPU and compatible Vulkan/ROCm backends; XDNA2 NPU requires supported compiled models and should not be treated as a transparent GGUF accelerator.

pricing.note: Advantech exposes Buy Online/distributor routing, but no stable public unit price was captured.

hardware.product: SOM-6874 with AMD Ryzen AI Embedded P185
hardware.memory_bandwidth_note: Derived theoretical peak from dual-channel DDR5-5600; not an application benchmark.
interfaces: PCIe Gen4 PEG up to x8
hardware.input_power: 4.75-20V module input; carrier design determines system input
hardware.llm_suitability: Useful rugged modular host for embedded local inference. 96GB RAM is enough for many large quantized models, while power and modularity are attractive for robotics and industrial nodes; bandwidth remains much lower than discrete HBM/GDDR accelerators.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Many 30B-class quantized models fit comfortably; selected 70B 4-bit-class models can fit subject to runtime/KV-cache overhead. Throughput depends heavily on backend and memory traffic.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: GGUF through CPU/compatible GPU backends; NPU use depends on XDNA2-supported model compilation/runtime.

pricing.note: No stable public retail price found; industrial COM Express modules are typically configuration/channel priced.

hardware.memory_capacity_note: Public page reviewed in this pass did not expose a defensible maximum installed-memory figure; capacity is intentionally left unspecified.
storage: 1x M.2 NVMe Gen4 x4 on carrier
additional M.2 NVMe Gen4 on COM
interfaces: PCIe Gen4 x8 in physical x16 slot
hardware.llm_suitability: Interesting serviceable/rugged x86 edge platform. Faster LPCAMM2/LPDDR5X-class memory can improve CPU/iGPU inference relative to ordinary DDR5 boards, but exact LLM throughput and installed-memory capacity require configuration-specific validation.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Configuration-dependent because SolidRun's public page did not provide a verified maximum RAM capacity in this pass.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: CPU and compatible GPU backends can use common quantized formats such as GGUF; XDNA2 acceleration remains model/runtime specific.

pricing.note: SolidRun states the platform is available now, but no stable public configuration price was exposed.
